Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS 13066. 1965 

Indian Standard 

CODE FOR SEAWORTHY 

PACKAGING OF COTTON HOSIERY 

YARN AND GOODS 

0* FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu* 
tion on 14 April 1965, after the draft finalized by the Cotton Hosiery and 
Knitted Garments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council. 

0*2 Packaging plays a very important part in preventing damage in hand- 
ling and in the safe transport of goods, their storage and marketing. Pro* 
per packaging with quality packing materials protects the goods mm the 
hazards of transit, provides for ease of handling and preserves the contents 
from infestation, contamination and other deterioration. This codk gives 
details of seaworthy paclutging of cotton hosiery yam and goodi which 
would ensure adequate protection to' the contents of the packages which are 
to be shipped overseas. 

0.3 Hosiery goods, especially of superior quality are often sent liirough 
post parcel, particularly w^en early delivery of goods are required^ This 
code gives the details of packaging hosiery goods in such cases aht^ 

0*3«1 The goods intended to be sent through post parcel are packed 
in cardboard boxes; the size and weight of such cardboard box shipuld be 
in conformity with the international postal rules and reguljatibhs. ^* 



U SCOPE -^ 

1.1 This code prescribes the method of packaging of cotton hosiery yum and 
goods for overseas markets.

bundte securely with cotton twine at least at three (daces iat right angles to 
the Uncigth of .the hanks. Wrap, each bundle in kraft papers Place pieces 
of cardboard of suitable sizes, one each on top and bottom of the bundle so 
as to form a rectajfigular bundle and tie it securely with cotton or jute t%irine 
of suitable qui^lily*

2.1JI When the bale is stilt under pressure, sew the layer of light weight

ped in pieces of hessian. 

2.2 Hosiery Ymrn ( Cones ) in Cases 

r 

2*2*1 Wrap each cone with kraft paper. Place a sufficient number of cones 
in a wooden packing case conforming to the requirements of A-3, and lined 
with one layer of waterproof paper conforming to Type 1 of IS : 1398- 
1960* and one layer of medium weight hessian conforming to Type I 
(305 g/m*) of IS : 2818-1964t so that when the case is fully lined up, the 
waterproof paper forms the inner layer and the medium weight hessian 
forms the outer layer. . The packing materials shall be of sufficient size to 
fiiUy cover the contents of the case. They shall be in sound, clean tod 
dry condition. If necessary, stuff the voids in the case with paper cuttings 
so as to prevent undue movement of the contents. 

NoTX— - To facilitate itjentification, each cone may be marked with the 'name of the 
material, name and tradthmark of the manufacturer, count of yam and noininal weight 
of the cone. 

2*2*2 The gross weight of the case shall not exceed 150 kg in weight. 

2«2.3 Fold neallythe layer of waterproof paper over the contents of the 
case to have adequate overlaps. Fold also the layer of medium weight 
hessian over the layer of waterproof paper. Stitch the ends of h|ssian with 
two strands of jute twine of suitable quality. Nail the lid to the citse. Bind 
the case with 0-9 mm thick and minimum 16 mm wide new *hardf grade flat 
steet strips ( or hoops ) conforming to the requirements of A-2i #> that: 

a) at least three strips are positioned parallel to the battens, 

b) at least two strips are positioned at right angles to the battens, and 

c) the strips are drawn taut and the twt) ends of each fiistened by 
rivets and/or other suitable means.

2.4 Hosiery Goods ( Garments ) in Gases 

2*4«1 If the goods consist of items, such as socks, stockings, etc, which are 
sold in pairs, fold the two units of the pair together and place a number of 
such folded pairs in a cardboard box of stiitable size. It the goods consist 
of other items such as vests, jerseys, etc, fold each garment suitably and 
place a suflScient number of them in a cardboard box. Close the lid of the 
box securely. 

2,4J[ Place a required number of cardboard boxes in a wooden packing

and the waterproof paper ( or polyethylene film ) forms the outer layen

cotton twine.

3. MARKING t 

S«l Bales, cases and cardboard boxes shall be marked on at least tw.^ 
opposite sides with indelible ink, with the following information, leaving 
adequate q>ace fiir marking by railways and postal authorities: 

a) Leading mark ( consignee's name, or initials ); 

b) Port of entry and destination, if other than port of entry; 

c) Serial number and total number of packages in the consignment; 

d) Gross weight and net weight of the package; 

e) Dimensions of the packa;ge; 

f) Manufacturers* name, initials' or trade*mark and 'country of 
origin; 

g) Handling mark, such as 'Use No Hooks* {sa Note ); 

h) Name of the material and indent number ( i( required ); and 

j) Any other information required by the buyer or by the law in 
force. 

NoOT — Thiff msrk it applieable only in the case of bales. 

3Jt All markings shall be stencilled, writing with hand being not Dermis* 
sible. In the case of bales and cases, the markings 3.1 (a) and {b)%Ml 
be not less than 8 em in height and the other markings shall be not less 
than 4 cm in height. 

SiSLl For post parcels, however, marking shall be legibly written by 
hand with the letters and figures of not less than 1 cm in height.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 AUGUST 1966 

TO 

IS ; 3086-1965 CODE FOR SEAWORTHY PACKAGING 
OF COTTON HOSIERY YARN AND GOODS 

At the draft stage, IS : 2771-1965 ' Specification for corrugated fibre- 
board boxes' included requirements for boxes made of solid fibreboard. 
Therefore, this standard prescribed solid fibreboard conforminfj^ to the 
requirements of IS: 2771 wiiich was then under preparation. As 
18:2771-1965, when published, tdid not cover boxes made of solid fibre- 
board, modifications in 2.5.2 and A-4 of this standard have now been made 
throui^h this Amendment. Opportunity has also been taken to rectify 
some errors in Table 1 and 2.4.2. 



Corrigenda 

( Page 4, Table 1, 5/ JVa. 1, last column ) — Substitute * Grade 123 of 
IS : 2508-1963t ' for ' Grade 213 of IS : 2508.1963t '. 

( Page 6, Table 2, SI No. 2, last column ) — Substitute • Grade 123 of 
IS : 2508-l963t ' for * Grade 213 of IS : 2508.1963t '. 

( Clause 2.4.2, line 8 ) — Substitute ' Grade 123 of IS : 2508.19631 ' 
for ' Grade 213 of IS : 2508-1963 J •, 

( Clause 2.5.2, lines 5 and 6) — Substitute ' Grade 123 of IS : 2508- 
1963*'* for ' Grade 213 of IS : 2508- 1963* '. 

Alterations 

{ Clause 2.5*29 second sentence) — Substitute the following for the 
existing sent<!nce:, 

• Arrange a required number of polyethylene bags in a suitable card- 
board box of suitable size and lined with one layer of polyethylene 
film or waterproof paper. * 

( Page 9, clauses A-4, A-4.1 and A-4.2 ) — Delete the clauses and the 
foot-note marked with double dagger (J) at the bottom of the page.
